new:
Adapters may own executable discovery, provider authentication, launch arguments,
environment placement, and provider diagnostics. They do not own authoring
semantics, GameEngine permission policy, work-claim policy, completion gates, or
canonical project persistence.

Provider discovery and session opening are allowed to block internally because they
may launch processes, start a Managed Local endpoint, and wait for ACP initialize or
session negotiation. A presentation thread must therefore never call those blocking
operations directly. AI Studio prepares the immutable Agent Host binding first, runs
discovery and `AcpAgentRuntime::open_session` on a process-local startup worker, and
only attaches the opened session after the bridge revalidates the original
`AgentSession` / `AgentRun` identity. Cancellation or a stale completion must cancel
and close any late-opened session so provider processes, Managed Local endpoint
leases, and ephemeral configuration cannot outlive the request that owned them.

### 10. Managed Local Agent Harness benchmarks normally use Goose ACP
